video_title: The Next Trillion Dollar Crypto Opportunity with Anthony B. (Coinbase Asset Management)
gist: The head of Coinbase Asset Management argues crypto is mid-bear (Bitcoin ~$64-67k in late July 2026, roughly 50% off the November 2025 peak of $126k) with funding rates just turning positive as a bottoming signal, and that the next cycle's money is in onchain asset management: Bitcoin-collateral yield strategies, stablecoin-funded hybrid credit that arbs tokenized versus traditional paper, and vault infrastructure that regulated managers are about to flood into. He also argues the fat protocol thesis is losing, with value accruing to licensed distribution platforms rather than tokens.

insights.claim: Bitcoin peaked at $126,000 in November 2025 and as of late July 2026 trades around $64,000-$67,000, roughly 50% below the cycle top.
insights.speaker: Anthony B. (Coinbase Asset Management)
insights.so_what: Sets the reference frame for drawdown math: a ~50% decline from peak is in line with prior Bitcoin cycles rather than a structural break.
insights.quote: we absolutely peaked in November of last year 2025 126,000

insights.claim: The consensus call in 2025 that Bitcoin's four-year cycle was dead and replaced by a five-year cycle has been proven wrong by the current drawdown.
insights.speaker: Anthony B. (Coinbase Asset Management)
insights.so_what: If cycle periodicity still holds, the timing of bottoms and the next expansion can be modeled off prior cycles rather than treated as unprecedented.
insights.quote: the four-ear cycle's dead, the 5year cycle is the new norm was the big call. I I think we can stand here today and look back and say absolutely that's a wrong call

insights.claim: The market's expected Bitcoin bottom ranges from an extreme low near $35,000 to a softer bottom in the high $40,000s to low $50,000s over the coming months.
insights.speaker: Anthony B. (Coinbase Asset Management)
insights.so_what: Gives a concrete band for scaling into spot or writing puts, with the low end implying another ~45% downside from current levels.
insights.quote: Um the market expects the price range to be anywhere from on the extreme low ends 35,000 to a more soft bottoming, you know, maybe in the low 50s or high high 40s.

insights.claim: Bitcoin cycle lows typically print as sharp weekend wicks that recover five or six thousand points within a day, making them practically uncatchable for discretionary buyers.
insights.speaker: Anthony B. (Coinbase Asset Management)
insights.so_what: Argues for programmatic scaled accumulation or resting bids rather than waiting for a confirmed bottom; a limit-order ladder captures what discretionary timing misses.
insights.quote: those are typically very sharp candles or wicks that will go down on a Saturday and then recover five or 6,000 points the next day and you're not going to be able to catch it

insights.claim: Any investor who bought Bitcoin and held for three years or longer at any point across the past three or four cycles made money, including someone who bought the prior cycle peak around $60,000 and holds today at ~$64,000.
insights.speaker: Anthony B. (Coinbase Asset Management)
insights.so_what: The 'worst-case entry' framing is the core institutional sales argument for a first allocation; it reframes drawdown risk as duration risk.

insights.claim: Roughly $60-70 billion was raised in 2025 to fund digital asset treasury vehicles, with nearly all of it flowing into Bitcoin and creating insatiable buying demand that captured supply at the top of the cycle.
insights.speaker: Anthony B. (Coinbase Asset Management)
insights.so_what: Identifies the marginal buyer that drove the 2025 top; if that fundraising channel is closed, the demand function for the next leg has to come from somewhere else.

insights.claim: Institutional plumbing for Bitcoin (ETFs, futures, perpetuals, options, swaps, bank integration, trust structures and direct spot in brokerage accounts) is now fully live, which was not true in prior cycles.
insights.speaker: Anthony B. (Coinbase Asset Management)
insights.so_what: Deeper derivatives and access rails mean cycle drawdowns are more tradable and hedgeable, and support the case that the asset's structural adoption is decoupled from price.

themes.theme: Leverage Flush and Funding Rates as Regime Signal

insights.claim: The October 10, 2025 liquidation event wiped out more than $25 billion across multiple non-US exchanges and was the single big catalyst that started this bear market, analogous to FTX, Three Arrows, BlockFi and Celsius triggering the 2022 bear.
insights.speaker: Anthony B. (Coinbase Asset Management)
insights.so_what: Frames the drawdown as a leverage-structure event rather than a demand collapse, which implies recovery tracks the rebuild of leverage, not new narratives.
insights.quote: The funding rate the leverage wipeout in October of 10 October of 2025 was the big catalyst that sent us into this bare market.

insights.claim: Funding rates have been unattractive and at times deeply negative for the past six months but are now turning positive again, which the speaker treats as an important market bottoming signal.
insights.speaker: Anthony B. (Coinbase Asset Management)
insights.so_what: A concrete, free, daily-observable indicator: sustained positive perp funding signals strong hands are re-levering and the market-neutral yield trade is coming back.

insights.claim: The Bitcoin funding rate arbitrage trade (long spot, short perpetual or future) returned roughly 4-8% net from 2021 through 2024 and spiked into the high teens or low 20s for weeks or months at a time.
insights.speaker: Anthony B. (Coinbase Asset Management)
insights.so_what: Benchmarks what a market-neutral crypto credit or yield product must clear; returns are leverage-driven and mechanically collapse in bear markets.

insights.claim: The post-capitulation recovery period runs about two-plus years during which leverage builds consistently and persistently, making basis and funding a durable source of alpha rather than a spot bet.
insights.speaker: Anthony B. (Coinbase Asset Management)
insights.so_what: If correct, the window to deploy into market-neutral crypto yield vehicles is opening now and lasts roughly through the next cycle expansion.

insights.claim: Retail was burned twice over in this cycle, first on memecoins and then on unhedged funding-rate arbitrage that got liquidated in the October 2025 event, leaving a market of capitulated participants and stronger hands accumulating.
insights.speaker: Anthony B. (Coinbase Asset Management)
insights.so_what: Ownership rotating from levered retail to long-duration holders is the classic setup that precedes low-float upside in the next expansion.

insights.claim: Large Bitcoin holders with very low cost basis face only three options for liquidity — sell and take the tax hit and lose the beta, borrow against the coins and take on liability mismatch, or deploy the Bitcoin as collateral into income strategies — and the third is the fastest-growing demand.
insights.speaker: Anthony B. (Coinbase Asset Management)
insights.so_what: Defines a large addressable pool of idle, never-sell Bitcoin as the raw material for the yield-product category; whoever wins distribution to it captures a recurring fee stream.
insights.quote: The mantra in Bitcoin is never sell, right?

insights.claim: Coinbase Asset Management's Bitcoin yield fund runs three collateral strategies against client Bitcoin — harvesting options volatility premia by selling delta-managed puts and calls, capturing the basis and funding-rate spread, and cash-and-carry where Bitcoin collateral funds dollar borrowing reinvested into short-duration and high-yield credit at a positive net interest margin.
insights.speaker: Anthony B. (Coinbase Asset Management)
insights.so_what: A replicable blueprint of where 'Bitcoin yield' actually comes from — useful for underwriting any competitor product claiming BTC-denominated income.

insights.claim: Coinbase has fully integrated Deribit, described as the largest options exchange in the world, and runs its Bitcoin options premium harvesting on top of it.
insights.speaker: Anthony B. (Coinbase Asset Management)
insights.so_what: Vertical integration of the dominant crypto options venue into a US-listed exchange is a structural moat for manufacturing yield products at scale.

insights.claim: The strategy is deliberately built to combine procyclical sources of yield (funding rates, which only pay in bull markets) with countercyclical ones so that it can generate income through both bull and bear regimes.
insights.speaker: Anthony B. (Coinbase Asset Management)
insights.so_what: Single-source BTC yield products dependent on funding will show near-zero returns in bear phases; regime diversification is the differentiator to screen for.

insights.claim: Coinbase Asset Management launched a stablecoin credit strategy in April 2026 whose fund shares are tokenized with Superstate on Base, Solana and Ethereum mainnet, and which accepts subscriptions directly in stablecoins rather than requiring a bank wire.
insights.speaker: Anthony B. (Coinbase Asset Management)
insights.so_what: Stablecoin-native subscription removes the banking on-ramp friction that has kept crypto-native capital out of regulated funds — a distribution unlock worth watching for copycats.

insights.claim: The stablecoin credit portfolio is roughly 80% traditional off-chain structured credit — CLOs, trade finance, asset-backed securities and accounts receivable — and 20% tokenized credit, with 90 to 100 day liquidity and hundreds of underlying names per line item to strip out idiosyncratic risk.
insights.speaker: Anthony B. (Coinbase Asset Management)
insights.so_what: The 'onchain yield' in institutional stablecoin products is mostly conventional structured credit; investors should underwrite it as credit risk, not crypto risk.

insights.claim: Crypto-native credit is entirely floating rate while the vast majority of traditional credit is fixed rate and longer duration, and traditional credit funds simply do not function on chain, leaving two parallel unconnected markets.
insights.speaker: Anthony B. (Coinbase Asset Management)
insights.so_what: The rate-structure mismatch is the specific reason tokenized credit has not scaled; whoever solves fixed-rate on-chain issuance unlocks the larger pool.
insights.quote: Everything in crypto is floating rate.

insights.claim: The core alpha thesis is arbitraging the tokenized version of a credit instrument against its traditional version — holding one, the other, or both — the same way one arbs futures or options against equity.
insights.speaker: Anthony B. (Coinbase Asset Management)
insights.so_what: Points to a nascent, uncrowded basis trade between wrapper and underlying that only hybrid TradFi/crypto managers can currently run.

insights.claim: The fund deliberately selects credit originators who are themselves pursuing a tokenization pathway so it can eventually trade the on-chain leg of assets it already owns off-chain.
insights.speaker: Anthony B. (Coinbase Asset Management)
insights.so_what: Originator tokenization plans are a leading indicator of where on-chain credit liquidity forms next — a screen for allocators and for infrastructure bets.

insights.claim: Tokenized credit instruments issued through regulated broker-dealers and transfer agents carry very little genuine smart-contract risk because US issuers must maintain an off-chain ledger, so if the protocol fails the asset can simply be reissued.
insights.speaker: Anthony B. (Coinbase Asset Management)
insights.so_what: Reframes the risk in regulated RWAs away from code exploits and toward leverage and forced-selling — a materially different underwriting checklist.

insights.claim: The real risk in on-chain tokenized credit is looping leverage across multiple DeFi venues and vaults, where an unwind in one place forces selling of positions in another, and the manager's edge is choosing to sit in the off-chain version and buy the on-chain version at a discount after the unwind.
insights.speaker: Anthony B. (Coinbase Asset Management)
insights.so_what: An explicit playbook: wait for vault contagion cascades, then buy the wrapper below the underlying — an event-driven trade only cross-market managers can execute.
insights.quote: I may choose to just wait for the unwind to happen in the onchain market and then go in and buy everything at a discount.

insights.claim: The tokenized credit opportunity is a rerun of the junk bond and high yield build-out from the 1980s onward and of early ETF NAV arbitrage, where a Millennium or Citadel pod recently posted roughly a $3 billion payout simply from arbing index rebalancing in the world's deepest equity markets.
insights.speaker: Anthony B. (Coinbase Asset Management)
insights.so_what: Argues new-market-structure arbitrage stays lucrative for years even in mature markets, sizing the prize for early tokenized-credit market makers.

insights.claim: Crypto investor demand is barbelled — investors want either pure directional beta or fully market-neutral spread returns, with almost no appetite for the low-volatility multi-strategy and trend products that dominate traditional finance.
insights.speaker: Anthony B. (Coinbase Asset Management)
insights.so_what: Product designers and allocators launching middle-of-the-curve crypto strategies are aiming at a market that does not yet exist.

themes.theme: Fat Protocol Thesis and Where Value Accrues

insights.claim: Value in crypto is accruing to distribution platforms that hold the licenses and the customer relationship rather than to protocols and their tokens, which implies the fat protocol thesis is going away.
insights.speaker: Anthony B. (Coinbase Asset Management)
insights.so_what: Argues for owning regulated distribution and exchange equity over layer-one tokens as the way to express crypto adoption.

insights.claim: Protocols use their own tokens to pay customer acquisition cost, granting hundreds of millions of dollars of tokens created out of thin air to distribution platforms for priority access, which is the cheapest equity and lowest cost of capital financing available and does not accrue value back to the token.
insights.speaker: Anthony B. (Coinbase Asset Management)
insights.so_what: Explains structurally why token holders are diluted by growth: the growth is literally paid for with the token, and the same mechanism lets any better-funded rival displace the incumbent.
insights.quote: So their the customer acquisition cost is actually paid for with tokens, right? that were created out of thin air based off of the initial value of the company raised

insights.claim: Protocols reliably grow TVL, usage, customers and assets into the tens of billions without ever demonstrating a point at which a consistent revenue stream returns to the protocol.
insights.speaker: Anthony B. (Coinbase Asset Management)
insights.so_what: TVL and usage metrics should be discounted heavily in token valuation until a revenue-capture mechanism is demonstrated.
insights.quote: where does the revenue switch turn on, right? How do you prevent yourself from getting displaced by the next competitor who has a better uh who has a new token that they've raised

insights.claim: There is an inherent tension between crypto protocols being public goods that should be nearly free, fast and efficient and the fat protocol expectation that they capture enormous value.
insights.speaker: Anthony B. (Coinbase Asset Management)
insights.so_what: A first-principles reason to expect protocol fee compression, and to look for value capture at the application and distribution layer instead.

insights.claim: The counterweight to protocol pessimism is that in this bear market a set of protocols that historically served only crypto natives are being integrated into fintechs and large brokerage houses serving hundreds of millions of customers.
insights.speaker: Anthony B. (Coinbase Asset Management)
insights.so_what: Enterprise integration during a bear market is the signal to watch for which protocols survive to monetize in the next cycle.

insights.claim: The bear market has produced a string of company shutdowns including Movement Labs closing after raising roughly $3 billion and multiple exchanges shutting their doors, with wealth created for a few founders but not for token holders broadly.
insights.speaker: Anthony B. (Coinbase Asset Management)
insights.so_what: Concrete evidence that capital raised in the last cycle was destroyed rather than compounded, tightening the bar for early-stage crypto venture underwriting.

themes.theme: Onchain Asset Management, Vaults and Regulation

insights.claim: The next crypto cycle will be defined by onchain asset management and by resolving what it means to be a fiduciary for customers on chain.
insights.speaker: Anthony B. (Coinbase Asset Management)
insights.so_what: The speaker's single highest-conviction forward call and his stated most-anticipated theme for 2027; positions infrastructure and regulated managers as the trade.
insights.quote: The next cycle is going to be defined by onchain asset management

insights.claim: Over the next few months a continuation of large regulated asset managers with compliance infrastructure and licenses will enter onchain asset management, bringing regulated processes into DeFi and reigniting a crypto-versus-TradFi fight over custody and discretion.
insights.speaker: Anthony B. (Coinbase Asset Management)
insights.so_what: Names the specific institutions to watch — JPMorgan has already announced its own vault on Kinexys, Bitwise is active and Grayscale has announced onchain asset management — as the near-term catalyst set.

insights.claim: Vault architecture is an orders-of-magnitude improvement over traditional fund administration, which is too slow for markets that now trade 24/7/365, and the entire asset management industry from BlackRock down accepts that vault infrastructure must become part of core investment management.
insights.speaker: Anthony B. (Coinbase Asset Management)
insights.so_what: Frames incumbent fund administrators as the disrupted party and vault tooling as an infrastructure category with a forced-adoption tailwind.
insights.quote: Everyone recognizes in the asset management community from Black Rockck down that we need vault infrastructure. It has to be a part of the core investment management landscape.

insights.claim: A vault is fundamentally just a stack of composable token standards — the speaker cites 4626 and 7744 and credits Centrifuge as a pioneer in launching them — each compounding on the last to replicate real-time pricing, NAV and attribution that TradFi does manually.
insights.speaker: Anthony B. (Coinbase Asset Management)
insights.so_what: The standards layer, not any single vault brand, is where the durable network effect sits; Centrifuge is named as the leader in defining it.

insights.claim: The unresolved regulatory question is whether a vault curator writing smart-contract allocation logic is exercising investment discretion and thus acting as a fiduciary, or merely giving buyer-beware advice.
insights.speaker: Anthony B. (Coinbase Asset Management)
insights.so_what: The single biggest legal overhang on DeFi vault economics; a discretionary ruling would force curators into registration and reshape who can run them.

insights.claim: Hester Peirce's recent comments on vaults were deliberately non-definitive and invited industry dialogue, a treatment the industry did not receive under the Gensler era, though her term is expected to end by year-end.
insights.speaker: Anthony B. (Coinbase Asset Management)
insights.so_what: The regulatory opening on vaults may be personnel-dependent and time-limited; the window for favorable rulemaking could close with her departure.

insights.claim: A specific unresolved conflict is that US advisers must hold client securities at a qualified custodian, which has no clean answer once tokenized securities move on chain into permissionless vaults or self-custodied wallets.
insights.speaker: Anthony B. (Coinbase Asset Management)
insights.so_what: Custody rules are the practical bottleneck that will determine whether regulated managers can hold tokenized assets on chain at all.

insights.claim: Even once the Clarity Act goes live it will take a very long time for firms to decide whether to issue tokenized versus traditional equity and whether to raise on-chain or through traditional capital markets, comparable to how firms are still working through Dodd-Frank integrations from 2009.
insights.speaker: Anthony B. (Coinbase Asset Management)
insights.so_what: Tempers expectations for a legislative catalyst trade — passage is not adoption, and the tokenization revenue ramp is a multi-year story.

insights.claim: Institutional investors are structurally forced to minimize cash because their only real mandate is to beat inflation, beat money supply growth and outpace their liabilities, and the majority fail at all three and end up underfunded.
insights.speaker: Anthony B. (Coinbase Asset Management)
insights.so_what: The debasement-hurdle framing is the actual sales wedge for Bitcoin into pensions; it reframes BTC as a liability-matching tool rather than a speculative sleeve.
insights.quote: the number one thing is can you beat monetary debasement and can you pay off your liabilities

insights.claim: Bitcoin is the only asset other than gold that combines fixed supply, global access and a monetary debasement offset, and it has now proven a better return than equity markets and other asset classes.
insights.speaker: Anthony B. (Coinbase Asset Management)
insights.so_what: The specific comparative claim underpinning pension allocation pitches; the whole case rests on the fixed-supply plus liquid-access combination that gold alone shares.

insights.claim: Private equity and venture, long treated as the best alternative for beating liabilities, are now oversaturated and likely face a decade or two of less than good performance.
insights.speaker: Anthony B. (Coinbase Asset Management)
insights.so_what: If institutions accept this, the allocation dollars leaving PE have to land somewhere — the implied beneficiary in his argument is Bitcoin and passive equity.

insights.claim: It is a great time to buy Bitcoin but investors should be selective about altcoins, taking only smaller allocations to the majors because it remains unresolved which networks will win and how tokens respond after the Clarity Act.
insights.speaker: Anthony B. (Coinbase Asset Management)
insights.so_what: An explicit BTC-over-alts allocation stance from an institutional manager at the bear-market lows, with token regulatory reclassification as the key alt catalyst.
insights.quote: Uh it's a great time to buy Bitcoin. This is not financial advice, but it's a great time to buy Bitcoin.

insights.claim: Asked to choose the biggest story of 2027, the speaker picks stablecoin credit over tokenized treasuries.
insights.speaker: Anthony B. (Coinbase Asset Management)
insights.so_what: Suggests the next leg of RWA growth moves up the risk curve from government paper into private credit — a directional bet on where tokenized AUM concentrates.

insights.claim: Privacy is the most underappreciated theme in crypto because most institutions do not want the market to see their movements or ping their wallets, though the right expression may be privacy built into architecture rather than owning privacy coins.
insights.speaker: Anthony B. (Coinbase Asset Management)
insights.so_what: Flags institutional transaction privacy as a prerequisite for large on-chain flows, and distinguishes the infrastructure bet from the token beta bet.
insights.quote: I think privacy is still vastly underappreciated and underfocused on.
